title: Introduce AuroraAttn unified kernel with rope-latch fusion and continuous-KV warmup
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Performance: Add AuroraAttn unified attention kernel with rope/rotary fusion and continuous KV warmup to improve short-request latency and throughput. Feature gated behind runtime flag.
description:
Motivation:

Serving latency for short chat-turn workloads and low-context embeddings has been a persistent pain point: KG and conversational flows see high P99s because attention hotpaths are not able to take advantage of fused rotary/rope transformations and warm KV state during continuous-batch scenarios. This PR introduces the AuroraAttn unified attention microkernel plus scheduler and KV-warmup hooks to reduce tail latency and increase throughput for mixed-length streaming loads.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new CUDA microkernel (aurora_attn) that unifies QKV concat, fused rotary/rope application, and a compact reduce-pass for attention score computation. The kernel is optimized for small- to medium-sequence lengths (8-256) where prior kernels paid overheads from separate rotary/precompute passes.
- Introduces a rope-latch mechanism: a lightweight precompute step which materializes just the rotary offsets needed for the current micro-batch and stitches them into the fused kernel to avoid extra memory traffic and repeated re-rotation.
- Adds continuous-KV warmup hooks in the serving continuous-batcher to prefetch and pin KV fragments for lanes that are likely to be reused within the next 20ms window (heuristic tunable). This reduces cold-KV misses and amortizes KV memcpy cost across micro-batches.
- Scheduler hints: extend the per-request routing policy to include an attn_cost_estimate and rope_affinity tag so requests are routed to nodes with prefetched rope/kv state when available.
- A runtime feature flag (runtime.experimental.aurora_attn) gates the new kernel and behavior; default is off for now.

Benchmarks (micro and e2e):
- Microkernel: measured on A100 80GB, fp16 accumulation. On sequences 16-64 and batch sizes 8-32, AuroraAttn shows 10-18% higher token/s vs existing fused-attn path and 20% lower P99 latency for single-turn requests.
- Continuous serving: in a 1000RPS mixed chat workload (70% short-turns, 30% long-turns) with continuous-batcher enabled, end-to-end median latency is ~8% lower and P99 is 22% lower after warmup stabilized. Cost-per-token estimated savings: ~6% due to reduced memcpy + fuse benefits.
